To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
on-chip thin-film TE modules can cool hot-spots by upto 11°C and harvest upto 85 mW of power from them.
it is possible for thin-film thermionic emission (TE) devices to provide 11°C of peak cooling at the chip hot-spots and to harvest upto 85 mW of power from them.
thin-film TE materials can be used for on-chip thermal management and energy harvesting with the potential to boost the clock frequency of a microprocessor by 33%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
evaluating the performance of on-chips TE devices for energy harvesting and cooling.
developing a comprehensive methodology to evaluate the workload dependent cooling and power harvesting capabilities of on- chip TE devices.
the evaluation of thin-films for the application of on-chip cooling/harvesting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
on-chip thermoelectric devices are a viable solution for on-chip power management and cooling.
on-chip thin-film TE modules can provide a viable alternative to on-chip cooling, and can potentially be used for energy harvesting as well.
the TE materials are indeed very promising for on-chip energy harvesting and cooling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TE materials are promising candidates for on-chip thermal management.
the recent advances in thin film TE materials are very promising for on-chip applications and can be effectively evaluated by our hierarchical simulation framework.
the on-chip TE cooling and harvesting can significantly improve the energy efficiency of the microprocessor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TE devices can be effective for on-chip thermal management and power-harvesting, but their design needs to be carefully optimized for the workload and the chip floorplan.

on-chip cooling/harvesting using TE modules are viable options for future microprocessors, and the design of TE modules needs to take into account the thermal profile of the chip and the workload dependent power consumption of the chip.
on-chip cooling can be achieved using TE modules without any major architectural changes, and can potentially be used for boosting the clock frequency and reducing the chip area of the processor.
